items.why: DID Core 1.0 §3.2.2 Example 9: "the relative DID URL value will be transformed to an absolute DID URL value of did:example:123456789abcdefghi#key-1"; RFC 3986 §5.2.2: an empty path with no query keeps the base path and query and takes the fragment.
RFC 3986 §5.2.2: an empty path with a query keeps the base path and takes the query.
RFC 3986 §5.2.2: query and fragment of the reference.
RFC 3986 §5.2.2: a path starting with "/" replaces the base path; the authority is method-name:method-specific-id (DID Core 1.0 §3.2.2).
RFC 3986 §5.2.3: "If the base URI has a defined authority component and an empty path, then return a string consisting of \"/\" concatenated with the reference's path".
RFC 3986 §5.2.2: path, query and fragment of the reference.
RFC 3986 §5.4.1: the empty reference resolves to the base ("\"\" = \"http://a/b/c/d;p?q\""); the base DID has no fragment.
RFC 3986 §5.2.2: a reference with a scheme is the target, so an absolute DID URL is not changed.
RFC 3986 §5.2.2: the dot segments of an absolute reference are removed.
